He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]] and was named the [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] for 2019. Hunter was selected in the [[2019 NBA draft]] with the 4th overall pick by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], but was then traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] before being traded again to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on draft night. He was traded during his sixth season with Atlanta to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and was traded again during the following season to the [[Sacramento Kings]]. ==High school career== Hunter grew up in [[Lawncrest, Philadelphia]] and attended [[Friends' Central School]] in [[Wynnewood, Pennsylvania]]. As a junior, he averaged 21.6 points, 11.0 rebounds, and 5.0 assists per game, while being named Pennsylvania Class AA Player of the Year. As a senior in 2016, Hunter averaged 23.5 points, 9.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.5 blocks per game. Hunter was rated as a four-star recruit and ranked as the 72nd overall recruit and 14th best small forward in the 2016 high school class.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/186502/deandre-hunter|title=DeAndre Hunter – basketball recruiting – player profiles|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date=April 25, 2016}} On September 12, 2015, Hunter committed to [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], choosing UVA over other offers from [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]].{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2565773-deandre-hunter-to-virginia-cavaliers-land-4-star-sg-prospect|title=DeAndre Hunter to Virginia: Cavaliers land 4-star SG Prospect|work=www.bleacherreport.com|access-date=September 12, 2015}} ==College career== [[File:De'Andre Hunter.jpg|thumb|upright=0.5|left|Hunter with [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] in 2019]] During his redshirt freshman season, Hunter scored double figures in 16 games, including in 11 conference games. During a game against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], Hunter scored the final 3 pointer to win the game at the buzzer.{{cite magazine|title=Watch: No. 1 Virginia Beats Louisville Despite Being Down 4 With a Second Left|author=Carroll, Charlotte|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/01/virginia-Louisville-buzzer-beater-crazy-ending|date=March 1, 2018|access-date=July 2, 2018|magazine=Sports Illustrated}} Hunter broke his wrist during the [[2018 ACC men's basketball tournament|2018 ACC tournament]] and could not play in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]].{{cite magazine|title=Virginia's De'Andre Hunter Will Miss NCAA Tournament Due to Broken Wrist|author=Rollins, Khadrice|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/13/virginia-deandre-hunter-miss-ncaa-tournament-broken-wrist|date=March 13, 2018|access-date=July 2, 2018|magazine=Sports Illustrated}} Without Hunter, the number 1 seed Virginia went on to lose in the first round to the number 16 seed, [[UMBC Retrievers men's basketball|UMBC]]. After this season, Hunter was named to the All-ACC All-Freshman team, as well as being named the ACC Sixth man of the year.{{cite web|title=ACC ANNOUNCES ALL-CONFERENCE TEAM, POSTSEASON AWARDS|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/2018/3/4/mens-basketball-acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards.aspx|date=March 4, 2018|access-date=July 2, 2018|website=theacc.com}} In his freshman season, Hunter posted 9.2 points and 3.5 rebounds per game. Hunter later announced that he would return to Virginia for the 2018–2019 season despite speculation that he could declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=De'Andre Hunter, who might have been a first-round pick in this year's NBA Draft, is returning to Virginia|author=Norlander, Matt|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/deandre-hunter-who-might-have-been-a-first-round-pick-in-this-years-nba-draft-is-returning-to-virginia/|date=April 20, 2018|access-date=July 2, 2018|work=CBS Sports}} In his sophomore season, Hunter averaged 15.2 points per game and 5.1 rebounds per game. He helped lead Virginia to another #1 seed in the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]]. Virginia would win the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|2019 Championship game]] 85–77 behind Hunter's 27 points and 9 rebounds, including a game-tying 3 with 12.9 seconds left in regulation. Following his second season, Hunter announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]], where he was taken 4th overall by the Los Angeles Lakers and later traded to the Atlanta Hawks.{{Cite news|url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-guard-de-andre-hunter-declares-for-nba-draft/article_dff48e18-5fb7-11e9-884d-1ff517e74fed.html|title=Virginia guard De'Andre Hunter declares for NBA Draft|work=dailyprogress.com|author=Josh Needleman|date=April 15, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2019–2025)=== On June 20, 2019, Hunter was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] with the fourth overall pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]], then traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in the [[Anthony Davis]] trade, and then again to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] along with [[Solomon Hill (basketball)|Solomon Hill]] for picks Nos. 8, 17, and 35 in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-draft-rights-to-deandre-hunter-solomon-hill-conditional-2023-pick-from-pelicans|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Draft Rights To De'Andre Hunter, Solomon Hill And Conditional 2023 Second-Round Pick From New Orleans|date=July 6, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 6, 2019}} On July 7, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] announced that they had signed Hunter.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-deandre-hunter|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign De'Andre Hunter|date=July 7, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019}} On October 24, Hunter made his NBA debut, starting in a 117–100 win over the [[2019–20 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]] and finishing with 14 points and two rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160656|title=Trae Young has 38 points, Hawks beat Pistons 117–110|date=October 24, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 24, 2019}} Hunter began the 2020–21 season in the starting lineup for the Hawks.{{Cite web|title=De'Andre Hunter 2020–21 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/huntede01/gamelog/2021/|access-date=2021-03-17|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}} On January 24, 2021, Hunter recorded a then-career-high of 33 points against the [[2021–22 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-hawks/deandre-hunter-has-career-high-33-points-in-hawks-loss-to-bucks/ZTAB4AHIDNHXTFYQPDYGTFERR4/|title=De'Andre Hunter has career-high 33 points in Hawks loss to Bucks|website=ajc.com|last=Spencer|first=Sarah K.|date=January 24, 2021|access-date=January 14, 2023}} On February 7, the Hawks announced that Hunter would undergo [[arthroscopy|arthroscopic]] surgery on his right knee and would be out for an extended period of time.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/hawks-forward-deandre-hunter-to-undergo-surgery-on-ailing-right-knee|title=Hawks forward De'Andre Hunter to undergo surgery on ailing right knee|website=nba.com|date=February 7, 2021|access-date=January 13, 2023}} Going into the All-Star break, Hunter posted averages of 17.2 points per game and 5.4 rebounds per game, leading to the NBA naming him to the Rising Stars roster.{{Cite web|last=Rowland|first=Brad|date=2021-03-03|title=Hawks forward De'Andre Hunter named to 2021 Rising Stars roster|url=https://www.peachtreehoops.com/2021/3/3/22301390/deandre-hunter-2021-rising-stars-roster-details-atlanta-hawks-nba-all-star-announcement|access-date=2021-03-17|website=Peachtree Hoops|language=en}} On June 9, the Hawks announced that Hunter would undergo surgery to repair a [[meniscus tear|torn meniscus]] in his right knee and would be out for the rest of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/hawks-deandre-hunter-out-for-season-with-torn-right-meniscus|title=Hawks' De'Andre Hunter out for season with torn right meniscus|website=nba.com|date=June 9, 2021|access-date=January 14, 2023}} On April 26, 2022, Hunter scored a career-high of 35 points and grabbed 11 rebounds. Despite his effort, the Hawks would lose the game 97–94 against the [[2022–23 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]], eliminating them from the playoffs in five games.{{Cite magazine|last1=Newton|first1=Matt|url=https://www.si.com/college/virginia/basketball/deandre-hunter-scores-career-high-35-points-in-loss-at-miami|title=De'Andre Hunter Scores Career-High 35 Points in Hawks' Season-Ending Loss at Miami|access-date=2022-04-27|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=April 26, 2022 |language=en}} On October 17, 2022, Hunter agreed on a four-year, $95 million contract extension with the Hawks.{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks & De'Andre Hunter Agree on Contract Extension |url=https://www.si.com/nba/hawks/news/deandre-hunter-agrees-to-contract-extension-with-hawks |access-date=October 17, 2022 |website=si.com|date=October 17, 2022 }} On January 13, 2023, Hunter scored 26 points on a career-high six three-pointers made in a 113–111 win over the [[2023–24 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |date=January 13, 2023 |title=Collins beats buzzer with tip-in, Hawks edge Pacers 113–111 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401468788 |access-date=January 13, 2023 |website=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} On January 27, 2025, Hunter matched his career-high of 35 points in a 100–92 loss to the [[2024–25 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/virginia/deandre-hunter-scores-career-high-35-points-sixth-man-of-the-year|title=De'Andre Hunter Scores Career-High 35 Points, Sixth Man of the Year?|website=Sports Illustrated|last=Newton|first=Matt|date=January 28, 2025|access-date=February 4, 2025}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2025–2026)=== On February 6, 2025, Hunter was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Caris LeVert]], [[Georges Niang]], three second round picks, and two pick swaps.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-deandre-hunter-250207|title=Cavaliers Acquire De'Andre Hunter|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025}} He made 27 appearances (five starts) for Cleveland over the remainder of the season, posting averages of 14.3 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. On November 8, 2025, in a 128-122 win over the [[2025–26 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]], Hunter received extensive media coverage for a play where he crossed over [[Josh Giddey]], causing Giddey to fall to the floor, and then finished with a two-handed dunk over [[Patrick Williams (basketball)|Patrick Williams]] in the third quarter of the game. Hunter finished the game with 29 points on 10-for-16 shooting, making 4-8 three-point attempts.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6790963/2025/11/09/deandre-hunter-josh-giddey-cavaliers-bulls-nba/|title=Cavaliers’ De’Andre Hunter ‘breaks’ Bulls’ Josh Giddey’s ankles with nasty crossover|last=Vardon|first=Joe|publisher=[[The New York Times]]|date=November 9, 2025|accessdate=November 9, 2025}} He made 43 appearances (including 23 starts) for the Cavaliers during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 14.0 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 2.1 assists.{{Cite web|title=De'Andre Hunter 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065732/deandre-hunter|access-date=March 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Sacramento Kings (2026–present)=== On February 1, 2026, Hunter was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Chicago Bulls]] which sent [[Emanuel Miller (basketball)|Emanuel Miller]], [[Dennis Schröder]] and [[Keon Ellis]] to Cleveland.{{Cite web |date=2026-02-01 |title=Kings Acquire De'Aandre Hunter In Three-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-deaandre-hunter-in-three-team-trade |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US}}{{Cite web|title=Cavaliers trade Hunter to Kings for Schroder, Ellis|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47793616/sources-cavs-trade-hunter-kings-schroder-ellis|website=espn.com|date=January 31, 2026}} In his second game with Sacramento on February 6, Hunter departed the contest after being inadvertently poked in the left eye by [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]] guard [[Kobe Sanders]]; he was subsequently diagnosed with [[retinal detachment]].{{Cite web|title=Kings Injury Woes Mount: De'Andre Hunter Out for Season|url=https://www.si.com/nba/kings/onsi/sacramento-kings-news/kings-injury-woes-mount-de-andre-hunter-out-for-season|access-date=February 23, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}} On February 20, it was announced that Hunter would require season-ending surgery to address the malady.{{Cite web|title=De'Andre Hunter has eye surgery, Kings' latest out for season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47990846/kings-f-deandre-hunter-season-left-eye-surgery|access-date=February 23, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
